question: Do the current workflow_run artifact validation and capability checks sufficiently prevent attacker-controlled artifact bytes from reaching credentialed state publication in every CodeQL-flagged path?
rationale: The PR deliberately creates new trust boundaries between credential-isolated producers and privileged collectors; static alerts cannot determine whether the repository-specific run identity, artifact binding, and schema checks are sufficient for the intended threat model.

options.title: Verify each trust chain
options.body: Require an alert-by-alert walkthrough or focused proof showing producer SHA, run attempt, artifact identity, manifest, digest, and schema checks all complete before any credentialed mutation.

options.title: Split privileged collectors
options.body: Land non-privileged ledger instrumentation first and move workflow_run artifact import and state publication into a narrower security-reviewed follow-up.

options.title: Accept monitored rollout
options.body: Accept the current mitigations and merge with explicit monitoring and rollback ownership for the first production lifecycle runs.

recommendation.title: Verify each trust chain
recommendation.body: Require an alert-by-alert walkthrough or focused proof showing producer SHA, run attempt, artifact identity, manifest, digest, and schema checks all complete before any credentialed mutation.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most strongly connects this person to repair workflow credentials, artifact handling, publication boundaries, and operational rollout behavior.
